name: Fullstack App | Paris 2024
tagline: Fullstack e-ticket platform handling authentication, payments, and secure user flows in production-like conditions.
popTagline: Built to explore full-stack application design, from authentication and payments to end-to-end integration.
popOverview: A full-stack online ticketing application for the 2024 Olympic Games, built as a study project. Visitors buy their tickets online and receive them by email as QR codes.

sectionKeyPoints.Shopping: Offers, cart and authentication, with the cart kept across sessions and merged on login.

sectionKeyPoints.E-tickets: Stripe payments, then a user key and a ticket key concatenated into a QR code sent by email.

sectionKeyPoints.Administration: An admin panel to manage offers and view sales statistics, and scheduled jobs for expired token cleanup and account deletion.

sectionKeyPoints.Business rules on the server: The backend validates carts and orders, handles payments and tickets, and enforces access rules; the frontend focuses on presentation and interaction.

sectionKeyPoints.API-first approach: Frontend development was guided by explicit API contracts, designed around its needs but generic enough to avoid tight coupling.

sectionKeyPoints.Nx monorepo: Angular client, NestJS server and shared libraries, with TypeScript interfaces shared across the full stack.

sectionKeyPoints.Consistent user state: An anonymous cart had to be merged with the account's cart on login, without duplicating or losing items.

sectionKeyPoints.Frontend–backend drift: Tightening API contracts and being explicit about response shapes reduced regressions.

sectionKeyPoints.Security and performance: An ORM prevents SQL injections and eases migrations, while indexes and custom SQL queries improve performance.
